I am getting the same error and all of my packages are completely up to date.

beast_file <- system.file("examples/MCC_FluA_H3.tree", package="ggtree")

pp <- (p + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0, 0.3))) %>%
    gheatmap(genotype, offset=8, width=0.6, colnames=FALSE) %>%
    scale_x_ggtree()

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I am having the same issue. I updated R to 3.5.1 and updated all of my packages. Rerunning a previously working R script to generate a plot of an ultrametric BEAST tree now has the same issue with 95% HPDs, the labels are offset to the right. If I plot it like you suggested (with "branch.length="height"") then it plots the HPDs correctly, however the plot I am generating should have all of the tips aligned as it is ultrametric. Something must have changed in package versions as the script I used is itself unchanged.

I have attached an example dataset with a copy of the older correct figure.

messages.subject_clean: geom_range not correctly displaying 95% HPDs for height from BEAST tree
messages.body_plain:
the branch length of your input tree is actually length instead of height.

This is the reason that all the bars are offset to the right of your code:
ggtree(mytree, right=TRUE, mrsd = "00-01-01") + geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', color='blue', alpha=.6, size=2)

If you change the HPD using length_0.95_HPD, it will works fine.

If you indeed want to display height_0.95_HPD, you need extra parameter as the following code:
ggtree(mytree, right=TRUE, mrsd = "00-01-01") + geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', color='blue', alpha=.6, size=2, branch.length="height")

> ggtree(mytree, right=TRUE, mrsd = "00-01-01") + geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', color='blue', alpha=.6, size=2)

messages.subject_clean: how to set x axis limits and title for the tree panel ?
messages.body_plain:
using ggtree v >= 1.13.4, we can use facet_labeller to label facet panels.
library(ggtree)
tr <- rtree(30)
p <- ggtree(tr)
d1 <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, location=sample(c("GZ", "HK", "CZ"), 30, replace=TRUE))
p1 <- p %<+% d1 + geom_tippoint(aes(color=location))
d2 <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, val=rnorm(30, sd=3))
p2 <- facet_plot(p1, panel="dot", data=d2, geom=geom_point,
 aes(x=val), color='firebrick') + theme_tree2()

lbs <- c(Tree = "tree panel", dot = "dot panel")
facet_labeller(p2, lbs)
